title: QUIC RFC 9000 Preferred Address Migration Source Protection Verification
verification_method: Focused S9P6P3-0006/0009/0010 requirement-home tests, Release build, full Release no-build solution tests, regenerated QUIC coverage triage, SpecTrace JSON validation, and whitespace diff checking.
scope: This verification covers the current single-active-path runtime behavior for same-family preferred-address validation, preferred-address changed-source protection, and probe-triggered validation on the S9P6P3 tail.
expected_result: The focused requirement-home tests prove that same-family IPv4 and IPv6 preferred-address candidates are validated before promotion, changed-source preferred-address traffic remains candidate-path and anti-amplification protected, and probe packets from a different address trigger a PATH_CHALLENGE without active-path promotion.
procedure: Run the focused S9P6P3-0006/0009/0010 requirement-home filter.
Run the full Release no-build solution test suite.
Check the resulting diff for whitespace errors.
preconditions: The runtime has an active path before preferred-address traffic arrives.
Peer transport parameters carry a preferred_address with IPv4, IPv6, connection ID, and stateless reset token values.
The connection has completed enough handshake state for active migration promotion to be policy-eligible.

supplemental_sections.heading: Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: This verification does not claim hosted endpoint interop, public migration APIs, or multipath behavior.

status_summary: Passed locally on 2026-05-04. The focused S9P6P3-0006/0009/0010 filter passed 5/5, generated triage resolves all S9P6P3 requirements as trace-clean, Release build passed with 0 warnings and 0 errors, the full Release no-build solution suite passed 4091/4091, core SpecTrace JSON validation passed for 382 artifacts, and git diff --check passed with only CRLF normalization warnings on regenerated/spec JSON outputs.
